blocks.content: The Right to Information Act of 2005 provides for the creation of not only the Central Information Commission but also a State Information Commission at the state level.

items: Selection Committee Composition: For CIC, it includes the PM (Chair), Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, and a Union Cabinet Minister. For SIC, it includes the CM (Chair), Leader of Opposition in Legislative Assembly, and a State Cabinet Minister.
Removal Procedure: Both Central and State Information Commissioners can be removed only after an inquiry by the Supreme Court on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
2019 Amendment Impact: Fixed 5-year tenure was removed; the Central Government now prescribes the tenure and service conditions for both CIC and SIC members.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Both the Central Information Commission (CIC) and State Information Commissions (SIC) are statutory bodies created under the Right to Information Act, 2005.
The CIC consists of a Chief Information Commissioner and up to 10 Information Commissioners appointed by the President of India.
The SIC consists of a State Chief Information Commissioner and up to 10 State Information Commissioners appointed by the respective State Governor.
The RTI (Amendment) Act, 2005 empowers the Central Government to notify terms of office, salaries, and allowances for both Central and State Information Commissioners.
Commissioners of both CIC and SIC are ineligible for reappointment to the same office after completing their term.
